title: Microsoft Teams: default meeting templates apply admin-chosen meeting settings to new meetings
summary: The default-template controls, Teams Premium requirement and rollout details are supported. The unrestricted statement that the feature takes no actions on its own is not documented; two supporting sources are missing, and several governance checklist controls have no table row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An administrator can set a custom meeting template as the default in a Teams meeting template policy.
claims.quote: After you create a custom meeting template, you can set it as the default in a Teams meeting template policy.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The default meeting template automatically applies when an organiser schedules a new meeting in the Teams calendar.
claims.quote: When an organizer schedules a new meeting in the Teams calendar or Outlook, the default meeting template is automatically applied.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The default meeting template automatically applies when an organiser schedules a new meeting in Outlook.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The default in a meeting template policy applies to new meetings scheduled by users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: When users who are assigned the policy schedule new meetings, the default template is automatically applied, retaining the custom template's default values and any locked or hidden meeting options.

claims.quote: Can't change meeting options that are locked.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact

claims.quote: Can't see meeting options that are hidden.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: The Global (Org-wide default) meeting template policy allows users to see all available templates by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Global (Org-wide default) meeting template policy allows users to see all available templates, including default templates and any custom templates that you've created.

claims.where: Governance controls: Global policy
claims.claim: The Global (Org-wide default) policy applies to users without another applicable policy.
claims.quote: If a user isn't directly assigned a policy or isn't a member of any groups that are assigned a policy, the user gets the global (Org-wide default) policy for that policy type.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/policy-assignment-overview to sources for the Global policy fallback statement.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting DefaultMeetingTemplateId to null applies no default template.
claims.quote: Must use the customtemplate_<GUID> format. When set to null, no default template is applied.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The default control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting template policies > policy > template > Set as default.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting template policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
In the list of templates, choose the custom template you want to set as the default, and then select Set as default.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity <policy name> -DefaultMeetingTemplateId customtemplate_<GUID> to set the default.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity Foobar -DefaultMeetingTemplateId "customtemplate_9ab0014a-bba4-4ad6-b816-0b42104b5056"
Sets the default meeting template that is automatically applied to ad-hoc or standard meetings created by users assigned this policy.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: The visibility control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting template policies > policy > Edit > Viewable templates > template > Hide.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and select Meeting template policies.
Select the policy you want to change, and then select Edit.
To make a viewable template hidden, select the template in the Viewable templates list and then select Hide.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity <policy name> -HiddenMeetingTemplates <HiddenMeetingTemplate objects> to change hidden templates.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity Foobar -HiddenMeetingTemplates @($hiddentemplate_1, $hiddentemplate_2)
Updates the hidden meeting templates array.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Template visibility and the default template are separate settings of the same meeting template permission policy.
claims.quote:
[-HiddenMeetingTemplates <PSListModifier[HiddenMeetingTemplate]>]
[-DefaultMeetingTemplateId <string>]

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Admins can configure custom templates with locked, hidden or editable options in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
Use this procedure to create a custom meeting template in the Teams admin center.
To prevent the meeting organizer from changing an option, select the option and then select lock.
To prevent the meeting organizer from seeing an option, select the option and then select Hide.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/create-custom-meeting-template to sources for configuring custom template options.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing a template as the default stops its automatic application to new meetings.
claims.quote: After you remove the template as the default, it's no longer automatically applied to new meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The feature takes no actions on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams default meeting templates automatically apply actions organizer unlicensed Teams Premium default template Outlook Mac web'; opened custom-meeting-templates-set-default and custom-meeting-templates-overview. Neither states this unrestricted negative.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'The feature automatically applies the configured meeting options when an organiser schedules a meeting.'

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls not represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Create the custom template', 'publish any sensitivity label', 'Check the Copilot setting', 'Assign the policy'. Table: setting a default and hiding templates.
claims.fix: Remove checklist steps for creating or adjusting template options, publishing sensitivity labels, checking the Copilot meeting policy and assigning policies: these controls have no corresponding table row. Do not add rows.
